name: fb-lane-coordination
description: FB is an open-source Codex plugin for Graph Engineering: it turns scattered AI conversations into a living product-delivery graph.

interface.longDescription: FB is an open-source Codex plugin that turns scattered AI conversations into a living product-delivery graph with six evidence-producing workstreams plus one Product/BFM control centre and seven pinned repository-scoped Codex tasks. $bfm executes only in Product/BFM, then stops at Ready to ship. Only Push Live authorizes merge or deployment; pinning never starts work.
defaultPrompt: Start here: use $fb-lane. Read bounded current status and current workstream cards first. When a task and question are known, call fb_project_context and open only its relevant cited authoritative records; retrieve completed history through archives, the handoff index, exact handoffs, QA evidence, and Git history only when needed. Run doctor if setup looks incomplete, show current status and active locks, then ask what outcome I want to deliver.

Treat FB as Graph Engineering for Everyday People. The graph is the repository-local delivery map connecting workstreams, decisions, evidence, dependencies, implementation, verification, and release state. Workstream loops move and learn inside it; $bfm navigates and executes it; Push Live authorizes release. Do not confuse it with a graph database, knowledge graph, or GraphQL.

Use $fb-lane to route evidence questions through User, Business, Design, Tech, Discovery, and Bugs. Product/BFM is the control centre, not an evidence-producing workstream. Each relevant workstream should investigate its question, gather evidence, recommend a path, and create a ready handoff MD file; record None relevant instead of inventing work.

On an explicit user request, a main workstream may send a queued fb-workstream-handoff to another. Tell the destination: <Source> handoff queued for <Destination> — planning only; waiting for you. Open: <handoff link>. Keep it idle until the user continues it; any delivery result needs a separate Product-ready handoff. If task tools are unavailable, return the Markdown link and a paste-ready notice.

Run $bfm only in the Product/BFM main task and only from the active canonical checkout. A ready handoff is queued for Product intake, not approval or execution. $bfm renders the complete intake ledger across User, Business, Design, Tech, Discovery, Bugs, and the separate Product/BFM control centre; dispositions every candidate; reconciles duplicates, contradictions, dependencies, locks, and the approved goal; then records the prioritized Build Brief before directing Codex implementation. Missing, unreadable, drifting, or contradictory intake fails closed through the canonical runtime.

$bfm automatically runs a cheap deterministic preflight. It selects Direct BFM only for one isolated bounded item with no graph-relevant signals. Multiple items, dependencies, conflicts, changed decisions, blocked or stale work, shared locks, applicable lessons, or release relationships select graph-driven orchestration. Report the route and reasons; never ask the user to choose. Missing, stale, or corrupt graph data uses the visible authoritative-record fallback.

When the approved Build Brief opts into the generic control loop, use deterministic routing before judgment, preserve the baseline, record flat clone-local evidence, compare named criteria, run distinct required gates, and keep configuration candidates isolated until exact Product approval.

After verification, use project-local continuous learning to record at most one provisional lesson per meaningful failure signature. Give later tasks only matching active lessons, confirm only after two helpful comparable applications, allow one revision, and immediately reject safety or must-pass regressions. Learning never resets Quick or Full repair budgets, executes treatment text, changes product or eval authority, crosses project boundaries, or authorizes release.

Own automated testing and bounded repair for the exact candidate. For Full BFM, use Product/BFM standing delegation to approve candidate-faithful changelog wording and authorize one release checkpoint without a user prompt. Ask only for changed product decisions, material scope, sensitive gates, or **Push Live**. Verify the Build Brief and Task Receipt changelog decision before reporting Ready to ship. Then say exactly: Automated checks passed. Optional review links are available above. Say **Push Live** to deploy. Never merge or deploy before Push Live.

When setup is requested, use $fb-setup. Treat Install or update FB from GitHub and set it up in this project. as the same setup intent after the plugin loads; the public GitHub entry point handles missing or outdated installation before this skill is available. It delegates to the canonical project-coordination-setup workflow for Codex only, preserves the fb-lane-coordination IDs and MCP paths, and uses six evidence-producing workstreams plus one Product/BFM control centre and seven pinned repository-scoped Codex tasks. Relay the one-time permission question for FB · Product/BFM, FB · User, FB · Business, FB · Design, FB · Tech, FB · Discovery, and FB · Bugs. After explicit Yes, reconcile only a proven-complete inventory for the verified exact project ID and canonical repository root: reuse and rename legacy sidebar tasks, create only missing tasks, pin all seven, verify them, and leave them idle. Product/User is a legacy User title; a lone legacy Product title maps to Product/BFM. Checkout moves use transactional migration: disposition every discovered difference, atomically record one canonical root, quarantine recoverable former roots, and rebind the exact seven tasks before retirement can be approved. Pinning never starts work. Use the honest manual fallback when inventory or native controls are unavailable. Then run doctor and report whether FB is ready.
